case_name: Baljit Singh & Ors. vs Tarseem Singh & Ors.
facts_of_case: Sh. Gurditta instituted a civil suit for possession of land against his children from both marriages. During pendency, Sh. Gurditta died and was substituted by his legal representative Sh. Tarseem Singh. The suit was filed to separate the parties' shares in the suit land.

legal_principles.principle: A co-owner in exclusive possession of joint property holds that property for and on behalf of all the co-owners unless a clear and unequivocal assertion of hostile animus causing ouster of one to other co-owners is demonstrated on record.
legal_principles.held: The Court held that co-owner in exclusive possession of joint property, holds that property for and on behalf of all the co-owners unless a clear and unequivocal assertion of hostile animus causing ouster of r to other co-owners, is demonstrated on record.

legal_principles.principle: A party claiming adverse possession must demonstrate a clear and unequivocal assertion of hostile animus causing ouster of one to other co-owners.
legal_principles.held: Simply because defendant No.1 had alleged raising construction over the suit land, his possession cannot be termed to be adverse against the other co-owners.
